name: reference_checker
description:
Verify an existing bibliography against Crossref: flags fake (AI-hallucinated), miscited and retracted references, one row per reference. Unlike citation_formatter, it judges whether a reference is real and accurate; it does not produce formatted styles. Use when you must audit a reference list, DOIs or titles before submission or review. Do not use to discover new papers (use literature_search or pubmed_evidence_table) or to restyle citations (use citation_formatter). Parameters: give bibliography, dois or titles (at least one). Lowering minMatchScore finds more but risks false matches; includeCandidates adds audit detail without extra charge. mode=monitor re-checks the DOIs/ORCID works against the state saved under monitorName and reports only new problems, so reuse the same monitorName on scheduled runs. Each reference checked is billed, so maxReferences/run_max_items cap cost on long lists. Returns per item: summary, status (OK/CHECK/FIX), verdict, matchedDoi, matchScore, mismatches (cited vs actual), integrity.status (retracted, corrected, expression-of-concern), openAccessUrl, warnings.

Behavior: read-only; runs the Apify Actor pandadad0214/reference-checker (https://apify.com/pandadad0214/reference-checker) on your own Apify account. Price: $0.01 per reference checked. Runs that find nothing are not charged per result, and spending is capped per call by run_max_charge_usd (default $0.50). run_max_items (default 50) limits items returned and fills maxReferences when you leave it unset, so it also limits what is billed; setting maxReferences higher can bill more than is returned. Most calls finish in 5-15 s for a few inputs; large inputs or crawls can take minutes, so raise run_timeout_secs (max 300) or shrink the input after a timeout error. Returns JSON {actor, count, items}; long text output is trimmed to whole items, with all items in structuredContent.

arguments.name: bibliography
arguments.desc: Bibliography / reference list. Paste a reference list in any common style (APA, MLA, Chicago, Vancouver, IEEE, Harvard). One reference per line, numbered ([1], 1.), or separated by blank lines.

arguments.name: dois
arguments.desc: DOIs. DOIs to check (bare 10.xxxx/..., doi: prefix or https://doi.org/ URLs).

arguments.name: titles
arguments.desc: Paper titles. Article titles to look up when you have no full reference.

arguments.name: minMatchScore
arguments.desc: Minimum match score (0-100). How close a Crossref record must be (title, authors, year) to count as found. Lower finds more but risks false matches. Whole number, 50 to 100; default 80.

arguments.name: checkOpenAccess
arguments.desc: Find open-access links. Look up free legal full-text links via OpenAlex. Default: on.

arguments.name: includeCandidates
arguments.desc: Include candidate matches. Also output the top Crossref candidates and their scores for each reference (useful for auditing). Default: off.

arguments.name: maxReferences
arguments.desc: Max references per run. Safety cap on references checked (each is billed). Whole number, 1 to 20,000 references; default 1,000.

arguments.name: contactEmail
arguments.desc: Contact email for Crossref (optional). Optional. Sent to Crossref as the mailto contact so requests use its faster 'polite' pool. Never shared elsewhere.

arguments.name: mode
arguments.desc: Mode. 'check' = the normal one-off check. 'monitor' = re-check the DOIs (and/or ORCID works) and compare with the previous run's saved state. Choices: check = Check references (one-off); monitor = Monitor DOIs / ORCID for new retractions (schedule it).

arguments.desc: ORCID iD (monitor mode). Optional. Monitor every DOI on this researcher's public ORCID record (plus Crossref works tagged with it), e.g. 0000-0002-1825-0097. Combined with the DOIs list.

arguments.name: monitorName
arguments.desc: Monitor name (monitor mode). Optional. Name of the key-value store in your account that keeps state between runs (letters, digits, hyphens). Use a different name for each list you monitor. Default: refcheck-monitor-, or refcheck-monitor.

name: citation_formatter

Convert DOIs, ISBNs, PMIDs, arXiv IDs, titles or messy reference strings into checked citations in APA 7, MLA 9, Chicago, Harvard, IEEE, Vancouver, BibTeX and RIS. Unlike reference_checker, it formats rather than audits: unresolved items are listed, not diagnosed as fake or retracted. Use when you need a clean bibliography or .bib/.ris export. Do not use to find papers (use literature_search) or to prove references are genuine (use reference_checker first). Parameters: pass references (one per line) or paste a whole list or .bib/.ris contents in text. All styles are one price, so request every style you might need in one call rather than calling again. Text lookups below minMatchScore stay unresolved; DOIs and IDs resolve exactly. Only formatted citations are billed. Returns per item: summary, status, one field per style (apa, mla, ...), inText, bibtex, ris, doi, title, authors, year, containerTitle; combined bibliography files stay in the run's Apify key-value store.

Most calls finish in 5-15 s for a few inputs; large inputs or crawls can take minutes, so raise run_timeout_secs (max 300) or shrink the input after a timeout error. arguments.name: references
arguments.desc: References (one per line). DOIs, DOI links, ISBNs, arXiv IDs, PMIDs ("PMID: 123"), paper titles, or messy reference strings in any style. Each one is looked up and formatted.

name: literature_search
description:
Search 250M+ scholarly works (OpenAlex) by topic query or seed DOIs and return ranked papers with DOI, citation count, free PDF link, retraction flag and a ready citation. Unlike pubmed_evidence_table (PubMed biomedical records with study design and PRISMA counts), this covers every discipline and supports citation-network expansion. Use when you need real papers on a topic, a reading list, or papers citing/cited by known DOIs. Do not use for systematic biomedical screening (use pubmed_evidence_table) or to find people (use researcher_expert_finder). Parameters: seedDois with no query walks the citation network per seedMode (citing = forward, references = backward); with a query it searches inside that network. searchIn=fullText broadens recall but lowers precision. retractedPapers=flag returns and bills retracted papers marked FIX; exclude drops them unbilled. sortBy changes dataset order only; readingListSize does not affect cost. Returns per item: summary, status, title, authors, year, venue, doi, citations, readingRank, readingScore, isOpenAccess, pdfUrl, retracted, citation, bibtex, ris, abstract.

Behavior: read-only; runs the Apify Actor pandadad0214/literature-search (https://apify.com/pandadad0214/literature-search) on your own Apify account. Price: $0.003 per paper found. Runs that find nothing are not charged per result, and spending is capped per call by run_max_charge_usd (default $0.50). run_max_items (default 50) limits items returned and fills maxResults when you leave it unset, so it also limits what is billed; setting maxResults higher can bill more than is returned. Most calls finish in 5-15 s for a few inputs; large inputs or crawls can take minutes, so raise run_timeout_secs (max 300) or shrink the input after a timeout error. Returns JSON {actor, count, items}; long text output is trimmed to whole items, with all items in structuredContent.

arguments.name: query
arguments.desc: Search query. Topic or Boolean query. Use quotes for phrases and AND / OR / NOT in capitals, e.g. "retrieval augmented generation" AND (clinical OR medicine) NOT survey. Leave empty to explore around seed papers only.

arguments.name: searchIn
arguments.desc: Search in. Title and abstract is the most precise (like a database search). Full text also matches papers that only mention your terms in the body. Choices: titleAbstract = Title and abstract (recommended); title = Title only; fullText = Full text (broadest).

arguments.name: seedDois
arguments.desc: Seed papers (DOIs). Optional. Start from papers you already trust. Combine with a query to search inside that network, or use alone. Up to 50 DOIs.

arguments.name: seedMode
arguments.desc: Seed mode. Which papers around the seeds to return. Choices: citing = Papers that cite the seeds (forward); references = Papers the seeds cite (backward); related = Related papers (OpenAlex similarity).

arguments.name: yearFrom
arguments.desc: From year. Earliest publication year (inclusive). Whole number, 1500 to 2100.

arguments.name: yearTo
arguments.desc: To year. Latest publication year (inclusive). Whole number, 1500 to 2100.

arguments.name: openAccessOnly
arguments.desc: Open access only. Only return papers with a free, legal full-text copy. Default: off.

arguments.name: minCitations
arguments.desc: Minimum citations. Only return papers cited at least this many times (OpenAlex counts). Whole number, 0 or more citations; default 0.

arguments.name: types

arguments.name: language

arguments.desc: Retracted papers. Flag keeps retracted papers in the results, marked FIX, so you know to avoid them (they are charged as returned papers). Exclude drops them before they are returned (not charged). Choices: flag = Flag them (FIX); exclude = Exclude them.

arguments.name: sortBy

arguments.name: maxResults

arguments.desc: Reading list length. How many top papers go into the ranked READING_LIST file. All papers are still in the dataset and exports. Whole number, 5 to 500 papers; default 25.

Choices: apa = APA 7th edition; mla = MLA 9th edition; chicago = Chicago author-date; harvard = Harvard (Cite Them Right); ieee = IEEE; vancouver = Vancouver (NLM).

name: pubmed_evidence_table
description:
Run one or more PubMed queries and return a screening-ready evidence table: one row per article with PMID, journal, study design, sample size, retraction status and citation, plus PRISMA-style counts for the whole search. Unlike literature_search (all disciplines, OpenAlex ranking, citation-network walks), this uses native PubMed syntax and MeSH and is built for systematic-review screening. Use when the question is biomedical/clinical and you need reproducible PubMed queries or design filters (RCT, meta-analysis, cohort). Do not use for non-biomedical topics (use literature_search), for trial registrations (use clinical_trial_leads) or to verify a reference list (use reference_checker). Parameters: queries accept PubMed field tags ([tiab], [mh], [pt]) and Boolean operators; several queries are de-duplicated into one table. Filters (studyDesigns, excludeAnimalOnly, hasAbstract, freeFullTextOnly, excludePreprints) run before billing, and PRISMA counts still report what they removed. retractedArticles=flag bills retracted rows marked FIX; exclude drops them unbilled. sampleSize is parsed from the abstract and comes with sampleSizeConfidence; treat low confidence as unverified. Returns per item: summary, status, pmid, title, year, journal, studyDesign, sampleSize, sampleSizeConfidence, retractionStatus, retracted, citation. Excel, PRISMA and RIS/Rayyan import files stay in the run's Apify key-value store.

name: grants_finder

Use when you need grants to apply for or want to see who was funded for a topic. Do not use for contracts (use federal_contract_finder) or small-business R&D topics (use sbir_sttr_topic_radar). name: researcher_expert_finder

Do not use for company contacts (use company_team_finder) or for papers themselves (use literature_search). Search official EU TED (Tenders Electronic Daily) public procurement notices through the TED Search API v3, with English title, publication date, buyer country, NUTS, notice and contract type, procedure, estimated or award value when published, tender deadline, CPV codes and TED HTML/PDF links. Unlike federal_contract_finder (US federal awards) and grants_finder (US assistance grants), this covers European public tenders. Use when BD or capture teams, EU suppliers or researchers need tenders by keyword, CPV code or buyer country. Do not use to submit bids, for US opportunities or for national portals outside TED. Parameters: daysBack (default 7) or publishedFrom/To set the window; keywords and cpvCodes (e.g. 72000000 IT services) match the notice; countries takes ISO-3 buyer codes such as DEU or FRA; maxResults caps billed notices. Value is often missing because many notices omit it. Empty input runs a small IT-services demo. Runs with no matches are free. Returns per item: agentSummary, noticeId, title, publicationDate, countries, nuts, noticeType, contractType, procedure, estimatedValue, deadline, CPV codes, noticeUrl, pdfUrl, htmlUrl; plus TED_XLSX/CSV.

Behavior: read-only; runs the Apify Actor pandadad0214/eu-ted-tenders (https://apify.com/pandadad0214/eu-ted-tenders) on your own Apify account. Price: $0.002 per notice returned. Runs that find nothing are not charged per result, and spending is capped per call by run_max_charge_usd (default $0.50). run_max_items (default 50) limits items returned and fills maxResults when you leave it unset, so it also limits what is billed; setting maxResults higher can bill more than is returned. Most calls finish in 5-15 s for a few inputs; large inputs or crawls can take minutes, so raise run_timeout_secs (max 300) or shrink the input after a timeout error. Returns JSON {actor, count, items}; long text output is trimmed to whole items, with all items in structuredContent.

arguments.name: daysBack
arguments.desc: Published in the last N days. Default 7. Searches publication-date >= today minus (N-1) days (UTC). Use 1 on a daily schedule. Ignored when Published from / Published to are set.

arguments.name: publishedFrom
arguments.desc: Published from. Optional YYYY-MM-DD. Overrides days back for the start of the window.

arguments.name: publishedTo
arguments.desc: Published to. Optional YYYY-MM-DD.

arguments.name: keywords
arguments.desc: Keywords. Full-text search. Each keyword becomes FT ~ "..." and they are joined with AND. Quotes are stripped. Example: software, cloud.

arguments.name: cpvCodes
arguments.desc: CPV codes. Common Procurement Vocabulary codes, e.g. 72000000 (IT services), 45000000 (construction), 33000000 (medical). Several codes are OR'd.

arguments.name: countries
arguments.desc: Buyer countries. ISO-3 country codes, e.g. DEU, FRA, ITA, ESP, POL, NLD, BEL, IRL, SWE. Two-letter codes (DE, FR, IT) are converted. Filtered server-side with buyer-country.

arguments.name: maxResults
arguments.desc: Maximum results. You pay per notice returned, so this also caps the cost. Default 200; hard max 2000.

arguments.name: run_max_items
arguments.desc: Optional. Most results to return from this call (default from PANDA_MAX_ITEMS, 50). Also limits how many results the Actor produces and charges for, unless you set its own max field.

arguments.name: run_max_charge_usd
arguments.desc: Optional. Hard spending cap for this call in USD (default from PANDA_MAX_CHARGE_USD, 0.50).

arguments.name: run_timeout_secs
arguments.desc: Optional. Seconds to wait for results (default from PANDA_TIMEOUT_SECS, 120; max 300).

name: broken_link_checker
description:
Crawl one or more start pages and check every unique http(s) link for HTTP status, final URL after redirects, a broken flag (status 400+) and a redirected flag, with external links checked by default. Unlike ai_search_seo_audit (page SEO/GEO scoring) and website_change_monitor (content diffs over time), this finds dead and redirecting links. Use when SEO, content or agency teams need a 404 report for a site or page. Do not use to search the web, to crawl a whole large site in one call or to check private or internal addresses (blocked and never billed). Parameters: startUrls (required in practice) are the pages crawled; maxPages is pages followed per host (1 = only the start pages); maxLinks caps checked links and therefore billing; checkExternal=false stays on-site; timeoutSecs is the per-request timeout (default 15). Billed per link that returns an HTTP status; timeouts, DNS failures and robots-skipped targets are free. Returns per item: agentSummary, originalUrl, finalUrl, statusCode, broken, redirected, external, contentType, sourcePage, error; plus LINKS_XLSX (all links plus a Broken sheet)/CSV.

Behavior: read-only; runs the Apify Actor pandadad0214/broken-link-checker (https://apify.com/pandadad0214/broken-link-checker) on your own Apify account. Price: $0.001 per link checked. Runs that find nothing are not charged per result, and spending is capped per call by run_max_charge_usd (default $0.50). run_max_items (default 50) limits items returned and fills maxLinks when you leave it unset, so it also limits what is billed; setting maxLinks higher can bill more than is returned. Most calls finish in 5-15 s for a few inputs; large inputs or crawls can take minutes, so raise run_timeout_secs (max 300) or shrink the input after a timeout error. Returns JSON {actor, count, items}; long text output is trimmed to whole items, with all items in structuredContent.

arguments.name: startUrls
arguments.desc: Start URLs. Pages to start from. The Actor fetches each page, extracts http(s) links, and checks them. Leave empty for a short demo on example.com. One URL per line.

arguments.name: maxPages
arguments.desc: Pages to crawl per host. How many HTML pages on the same host as each start URL to fetch for extracting more links. 1 = only the start URL(s). Further same-host pages are queued only when this is greater than 1. robots.txt is respected for crawl sources.

arguments.name: maxLinks
arguments.desc: Maximum links to check. Maximum unique http(s) URLs to check. This is what you are charged for. Hard max 2,000. (maxResults is accepted as an alias.)

arguments.name: checkExternal
arguments.desc: Check outbound (external) links. When on, links to other hosts are checked too. Turn off to check only same-host links.

arguments.name: timeoutSecs
arguments.desc: Per-request timeout (seconds). How long to wait for each request. Timed-out URLs are recorded but not charged.

arguments.name: run_max_items
arguments.desc: Optional. Most results to return from this call (default from PANDA_MAX_ITEMS, 50). Also limits how many results the Actor produces and charges for, unless you set its own max field.

arguments.name: run_max_charge_usd
arguments.desc: Optional. Hard spending cap for this call in USD (default from PANDA_MAX_CHARGE_USD, 0.50).
